title: Attacked by the Fighting Trees, part 1
attribution: From The Wonderful Wizard of Oz by L. Frank Baum (1900), via Project Gutenberg, in reading order.
body: The next morning Dorothy kissed the pretty green girl good-bye, and they all shook hands with the soldier with the green whiskers, who had walked with them as far as the gate. When the Guardian of the Gate saw them again he wondered greatly that they could leave the beautiful City to get into new trouble. But he at once unlocked their spectacles, which he put back into the green box, and gave them many good wishes to carry with them.
“You are now our ruler,” he said to the Scarecrow; “so you must come back to us as soon as possible.”
“I certainly shall if I am able,” the Scarecrow replied; “but I must help Dorothy to get home, first.”
As Dorothy bade the good-natured Guardian a last farewell she said:
“I have been very kindly treated in your lovely City, and everyone has been good to me. I cannot tell you how grateful I am.”

“Don’t try, my dear,” he answered. “We should like to keep you with us, but if it is your wish to return to Kansas, I hope you will find a way.” He then opened the gate of the outer wall, and they walked forth and started upon their journey.

The sun shone brightly as our friends turned their faces toward the Land of the South. They were all in the best of spirits, and laughed and chatted together. Dorothy was once more filled with the hope of getting home, and the Scarecrow and the Tin Woodman were glad to be of use to her. As for the Lion, he sniffed the fresh air with delight and whisked his tail from side to side in pure joy at being in the country again, while Toto ran around them and chased the moths and butterflies, barking merrily all the time.

“City life does not agree with me at all,” remarked the Lion, as they walked along at a brisk pace. “I have lost much flesh since I lived there, and now I am anxious for a chance to show the other beasts how courageous I have grown.”

questions.prompt: According to the passage, who walked with them as far as the gate?
options: The soldier with the green whiskers
The Guardian of the Gates himself
The pretty green-haired girl
Nobody went with them at all

questions.prompt: Per the passage, what did the Guardian do with their spectacles?
options: Unlocked them and put them in the green box
Locked them on again for the journey south
Gave each of them a spare pair to carry
Kept them and charged a fee for it

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the Guardian ask of the Scarecrow?
options: To come back to them as soon as possible
To leave the Golden Cap behind him
To send word from the land of the South
To take the soldier with him as a guide

questions.prompt: Per the passage, what was Toto doing as they walked?
options: Chasing moths and butterflies, barking merrily
Riding along inside Dorothy's basket
Walking close beside the Cowardly Lion
Sleeping in the Tin Woodman's arms

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the Lion say about city life?
options: That it did not agree with him at all
That he would gladly return to it
That it had made him stronger
That he had never minded it

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what puzzled the Guardian about them?
options: That they would leave a beautiful city for new trouble
That they had come back to the gate so soon
That the Scarecrow was leaving his own city
That Dorothy still wanted to reach Kansas

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why was the Lion glad to be out of the city?
options: He could breathe country air and had lost flesh indoors
He was afraid of the people in the streets
He wanted to be free of the Scarecrow's rule
He had been kept in a yard the whole time

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what does the Lion now want a chance to do?
options: Show the other beasts how courageous he has grown
Hunt for his own food again in the woods
Prove that he can outrun the Winged Monkeys
Find a mate among the beasts of the South

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does at a brisk pace mean?
options: Walking quickly and briskly along
Walking slowly, to save strength
Stopping often to look about
Marching in a straight line

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the passage?

A departure delayed by the Guardian's refusal to open the gate
A quarrel about whether the Scarecrow should leave his city
A sad farewell in which nobody expects to return

questions.prompt: According to the passage, whom did Dorothy kiss good-bye?
options: The pretty green girl
The Guardian of the Gates
The soldier with green whiskers
The Scarecrow

questions.prompt: Per the passage, what did the Scarecrow promise the Guardian?
options: To come back if he was able, after helping Dorothy
To send the Winged Monkeys to rule in his place
To return before the end of the month
To take the Guardian with him to the South

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the Guardian wish for Dorothy?
options: That she would find a way back to Kansas
That she would stay in the city forever
That she would send word once she arrived
That she would take the green girl with her

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, how did Dorothy feel as they set out?
options: Filled once more with hope of getting home
Certain that the journey would fail
Sorry that she had ever left Kansas
Indifferent to where they were going

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what pleased the Scarecrow and the Woodman?

Leaving the Emerald City behind

Curling it beneath him as he sat
Using it to wipe away a tear

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarises the passage?
options: A warm parting at the gate and a hopeful start on the road south

A journey that begins badly with a quarrel
